references.text: Abram elaborates on his concern, stating that since God has not given him offspring, a servant born in his house will inherit him – a direct continuation of the complaint in verse 2.
Abraham asks God to let Ishmael live before His face, reflecting his repeated concern about having an heir, as he expressed in 15:2.
Abraham tells his oldest servant, who manages all that he owns – traditionally identified as Eliezer of Damascus (Gen 15:2) – to find a wife for Isaac.

Stephen recounts that God gave Abraham no inheritance in the land, not even a foot's breadth, but promised to give it to his descendants – even though he had no children yet, just as Abraham complained about in 15:2.

By faith, Abraham received strength to become a father, even though he was too old, because he considered God faithful. From one man came descendants as numerous as the stars – an answer to the childlessness he lamented in 15:2.
The verses show a narrative progression from doubt about God's promise of offspring to a human attempt to hasten its fulfillment.
